title: Frequently Asked Questions – Western States 100
claims: The closest airports are Reno, NV (RNO) at 50 miles from Olympic Valley, Sacramento, CA (SMF) at 100 miles, and San Francisco, CA (SFO) at 200 miles.
There are accommodations near the start in Olympic Valley, the home of Palisades Tahoe ski resort, and also in nearby Truckee and Tahoe City.
The race does not provide a shuttle service back to the start; rides after the awards ceremony, Uber or Lyft can be used.
To enter the lottery a runner must have run one of the listed qualifying races, and there are no exceptions.
The lottery is held on the first Saturday in December in the auditorium at Placer High School, 123 Agard St., Auburn, CA.
Many checkpoints are restricted to race officials because of limited parking and the need to keep narrow access roads clear for fire and rescue equipment.
At the start, spectators can watch check-in and runner briefings on Friday and the 5:00 a.m. start on Saturday.
Robinson Flat can only be reached via the Foresthill Divide Road out of Foresthill, about an hour by road, with parking about a mile short at Sailor Bar and a shuttle bus to the aid station.

The FAQ spectator section says front runners reach Robinson Flat after about 9:00 a.m. and continue until the 1:50 p.m. cutoff, while the current official checkpoint chart gives a 2:10 p.m. cutoff at Robinson Flat.
Foresthill has plenty of parking in town and places to view runners; the latest time for runners to reach Foresthill is about midnight.
At the finish, the first runner may arrive as early as 7:00 p.m., 24-hour runners must arrive by 5:00 a.m. Sunday and 30-hour runners by 11:00 a.m.
Spectators are asked to stay within 1/4 mile of the checkpoints and not to provide food, beverages or other assistance outside the main checkpoint areas.
There is a 31-hour live broadcast on the event's YouTube channel.
Training runs are offered in late May during Memorial Day weekend.
